questions.question: The measurement of a kho - kho field must be _______.

• **Kho Kho** is one of the oldest games in the world, which was invented in **Maharashtra (India)**. 
 
• The origin of **Kho-Kho** is very difficult to know, but many of the **historians** assumed that it is a modified form of "**Run Chase**", which simply involves **Chasing and Touching a person.**
 
• In, **Ancient times** **Kho-Kho** was played on **"Raths" or "Chariots"**. It was known as "**Rathera". **
 
• A Kho kho playing field is rectangular in shape. It is 27 x 16 meters (89 ft × 52 ft) in length.

• In the middle of these two rectangles field, there are Two Wooden poles.
 
• The Central lane's dimensions are 24 m x 30 cm.
 
• It is an Outdoor sport and played by teams of Twelve(12) nominated players out of Fifteen(15) players, of which nine(9) players enter the field who sit on their Knees (Chasing team), and Three(3) players extra (Defending team) who try to avoid being touched by members of the opposing team(Chasing team).
 
• in 1949, the poles were firstly introduced in the game. Also, the Three(3) rounds at the beginning of the game were mitigated to one(1) round from pole to pole.
 
• The match of Kho-Kho consists of (2)two innings with each inning consisting of Chasing and Running Teams turns of nine(9) minutes each in the match.

• The **current captain of Kho-K ho India** is** Nasreen Sheikh (August 2020)**.

questions.question: During the British era Indian economy was known as ________.

options.text: a source for its raw material
only a market for agricultural products
a source for finished capital goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a source of its raw material **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the British era, I**ndia's economy was known as a market for agricultural products and a source of raw materials for British industries**.
 
• **British rule in India:**
 
• **Commercialization of agriculture**
 
 
• The British introduced cash crops like tea, coffee, indigo, opium, cotton, jute, sugarcane, and oilseeds.
 
• This reduced India's self-sufficiency in food. 
 
 
 
• **Negative impact on Indian industries**
 
 
• The British imported large quantities of products made by mechanical looms in England, which threatened Indian handicraft industries. 
 
 
 
• **Slow industrial development**
 
 
• The British did not establish a capital goods industry to support India's industrial development.
 
• They wanted Indians to depend on Britain for capital and heavy goods. 
 
 
 
• **Stagnant per-capita income**
 
 
• India's per-capita income remained mostly stagnant during the British Raj.
 
• Most of its GDP growth came from an expanding population. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The British Raj had a devastating impact on India's economy, leading to a decline in the country's share of the world economy: **
 
• **Trade**
 
 
• India's **exports changed from processed goods to raw materials, and imports changed from bullion to manufactured goods. **
 
• **The British used tariffs to limit India's exports of finished goods, while allowing raw materials to be exported freely. **
 
 
 
• **Agriculture**
 
 
• British economic policies led to a decline in agricultural yields and worsened the conditions of farmers. 
 
 
 
• **Povert**y
 
 
• The British used land revenue for war, leaving little for development.
 
• This led to widespread poverty and recurring famines. 
 
 
 
• **Infrastructure**
 
 
• The **British built railways to connect inland regions with exporting ports, which made trading easier and more profitable for the British. **
 
• **However, the railways were built to facilitate exploitation of the local Indians. **
 
 
 
• **Handicrafts**
 
 
• The British used discriminatory tariffs to undermine the Indian handicraft sector.
 
• The finished goods produced in the United Kingdom were machine-made and of higher quality and lower cost than the Indian handicraft ones. 
 
 
 
• **GDP**
 
 
• India's G**DP (PPP) per capita began to decline prior to the onset of British rule. **
 
• **From 1600 to 1871 the ratio of GDP per capita in India to that in Britain fell from more than 60% to less than 15%. **

questions.question: After which incident did Mahatma Gandhi call off the non-cooperation movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chauri Chaura Incident**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chauri Chaura incident:-**

 
 
• On February 5, 1922, a mob of protesters participating in the Non-cooperation Movement at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh, India, clashed with the police.
 
• The protesters set fire to the police station, killing 22 policemen.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-cooperation Movement in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre, also known as the Amritsar massacre, took place on April 13, 1919.
 
• On this day, around 50 troops of the British Indian Army, under the command of Colonel Reginald Dyer, fired on a crowd of Baishakhi pilgrims, who had gathered in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, Punjab.
 
• After a public outcry, the British Government formed the Hunter Commission to probe into the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre. 
 
• The Hunter Commission condemned the Massacre, but no action was recommended against General Dyer, who was responsible for the Massacre.
 
• Rabindranath Tagore returned his Knighthood in response to the massacre.
 
• Lord Chelmsford (1916-1921) was the Governor-General/Viceroy of India during the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre. 
 
• Governor Michael O' Dyer was assassinated by Udham Singh in London in 1940 as revenge against the massacre.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the collegium system?

options.text: This system started in the year 2007.
This system was evolved through Supreme Court judgment.
It recommends the appointments and transfers of judges.
It consists of Chief Justice and four senior judges of Supreme Court.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**This system started in the year 2007. **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This system started in the year 2007.
 
• **This is Incorrect**: The collegium system did not start in 2007.
 
 
• It evolved through judicial decisions in three landmark cases known as the **Three Judges Cases**:
 
 
• **First Judges Case (1981):** The executive had primacy in judicial appointments.
 
• **Second Judges Case (1993):** The judiciary established its primacy by creating the collegium system for judicial appointments.
 
• **Third Judges Case (1998):** Expanded the collegium to include the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and **four senior-most judges** of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• Thus, the collegium system became functional in **1993**, not 2007.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Collegium system:

 
• It is the system of appointment and transfer of judges that has evolved through judgments of the Supreme Court, and not by an Act of Parliament or by a provision of the Constitution.
 
• The Supreme Court collegium is headed by the CJI (Chief Justice of India) and comprises four other senior-most judges of the court.
 
• Judges of the higher judiciary are appointed only through the collegium system and the government has a role only after names have been decided by the collegium.

questions.question: Which of the tides have variations in height?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Mixed tide.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The tides having variations in height are known as Mixed tide.**
 
• The periodical rise and fall of the sea level, once or twice a day, mainly due to the** attraction of the sun and the moon, is called a tide.**
 
• **The moon’s gravitational pull **to a great extent and to a lesser extent the** sun’s gravitational pull,** are the major causes for the occurrence of tides.
 
• Another factor is** centrifugal force which acts opposite to gravitational pull of earth.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Diurnal tide**

 
 
• There is only one high tide and one low tide during each day.
 
• The successive high and low tides are approximately of the same height.
 
 
 
• **Semi- diurnal tide**
 
 
• The most common tidal pattern, featuring two high tides and two low tides each day .
 
• The successive high or low tides are approximately of the same height.
 
 
 
• **Neap Tide**
 
 
• A neap tide is a moderate tide that occurs when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other
 
• Neap tides have a tidal range that is usually 10 to 30 percent less than the mean tidal range

questions.question: Which of the following is considered to be the most liquid asset?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Money**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Money__ is the most liquid of all assets.
 
• A liquid asset is cash on hand or an asset that can be easily converted to cash.
 
• In terms of liquidity, cash/money is supreme since cash/money as legal tender is the ultimate goal.
 
• Liquid assets are often viewed as cash, and likewise may be called cash equivalents because the owner is confident the assets can easily be exchanged for cash at any time.
 
• Examples of liquid assets held by both individuals and businesses include *Cash, Money market assets, Marketable equity securities (stocks), Marketable debt securities (bonds), Accounts receivable, Inventory, etc.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***

 
• An asset which can be easily transformed into cash in less time and with no loss or little loss in value is known as a liquid asset.
 
• Liquid assets are usually compared with cash as the value remains the same whenever sold.
 
• These types of assets are commonly used by businesses and buyers.
 
• Liquidity describes your ability to exchange an asset for cash.
 
• The easier it is to convert an asset into cash, the more liquid it is.
 
• Cash or money is generally considered the most liquid asset.
 
• 
 
Cash in a bank account or credit union account can be accessed quickly and easily, via a bank transfer or an ATM withdrawal.

questions.question: In the year 2022, Arjun Singh Dhurve was conferred the Padma Shri for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?

• Arjun Singh Dhurve is a renowned Baiga dancer and has been actively promoting and preserving the Baiga dance form for over two decades.

questions.question: Which famous Chinese philosopher and scholar emphasised the importance of ethical values, family relationships and social harmony in his teachings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Confucius**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Asian scholar who, like Aristotle, supported the ethical concept of 'Golden Mean' as applied in communication was: Confucius**
 
• **Confucius, a Chinese philosopher, is known for his concept of the 'Doctrine of the Mean' or Zhong Yong in Chinese. **
 
• This concept has similarities to Aristotle's 'Golden Mean'. Confucius' Doctrine of the Mean advocates for moderation and balance in all actions, and cautions against actions that are excessive or deficient.

questions.question: Which method was used for making bronze statues during Harrapan Civilisation ?

__
 
• The **bronze statue** of a **dancing girl** from **Mohenjo-Daro** is a significant example of the prehistoric **Harappan Civilisation**.
 
• It was made using the technique known as** lost wax casting.**
 
• **Wax** is used to create a wax replica of the statue, which is then covered with a **cast** or mould.
 
• When the mould is **heated**, the wax drains out.
 
• The mould is then filled with **molten** **bronze**, which is then cooled.
 
• The metal statue is gradually revealed once the cast has been carefully broken.

Hence, the correct answer is **Lost Wax casting.**__

questions.question: The value of final goods and services produced in a country is known as _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**national income**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

__Key Points__

__
 
• The **value of final goods and services produced in a country is known as National income.**
 
• National income** refers to the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced w**ithin a country's borders during a specific period, typically a year.
 
• It **serves as a comprehensive measure of a country's economic performance and standard of living.**
 
• National income is often calculated using various methods such as the **Production Method**, **Income Method**, and **Expenditure Method**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

Additional Information__

 
• **Components**

 
 
• **​Production Method**

 
 
• This method calculates GDP by summing the value-added at each stage of production in various sectors.
 
• Value-added refers to the difference between the value of output and the cost of intermediate goods used in production.
 
 
 
• **Income Method**
 
 
• This method calculates GDP by summing all incomes earned by individuals, businesses, and the government within a country.
 
• It Includes wages, rent, interest, and profits. Additionally, it takes into account indirect taxes and subtracts subsidies.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Expenditure Method**
 
 
• **This method calculates GDP by summing all expenditures on final goods and services in the economy.**
 
• **It Includes consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports (exports minus imports).**

questions.question: Which physicist is known for extensive research in ‘radiation phenomena’ and the discovery of polonium and radium ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marie Curie**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Marie Curie is **the physicist known for her research into radiation phenomena and the discovery of polonium and radium.**
 
• She also contributed to cancer treatments. 
 
• Marie Curie, was a Polish-born physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity – a term she herself coined.
 
• **In fact, not only did she discover radium, but she also discovered another element, polonium, which she named after her native country, Poland.**
 
• Her work with radium began as a continuation of the research conducted by **Henri Becquerel**, who first discovered **radioactivity in uranium minerals**. Intrigued by Becquerel's work, the Curies proceeded to investigate uranium's properties and then expanded their research to other potential elements that exhibited the same behavior.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During their research, the Curies established that radioactivity wasn't due to interactions with other elements but was, instead, an atomic property.
 
• This was a groundbreaking revelation at the time and fundamentally changed the understanding of how atoms worked.
 
• From ore called pitchblende, which was known to contain uranium, they managed to extract trace amounts of a significantly more radioactive element, which they named radium.
 
• This discovery in 1898 confirmed their hypothesis that radioactivity was not unique to uranium.
 
• Marie Curie's work on radioactivity has earned her a host of prestigious accolades, including two Nobel Prizes: the Nobel Prize in Physics (which she shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel) in 1903, and the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1911.
 
• She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and she remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different fields of the natural sciences.
 
• Her contributions to science, particularly in the field of radioactivity, have made a significant impact on the world.
